---
title: "Plant-mPLoc"
description: "Submit a complete plant protein sequence to the public Plant-mPLoc service and record single- or multi-location predictions."
---

## Purpose

**Toolkits → Plant-mPLoc** predicts plant-protein subcellular localization from an amino-acid sequence. ProtVis submits the sequence to the public Plant-mPLoc academic server and parses one or more predicted cellular locations.

The current integration recognizes 12 location classes, including chloroplast, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondrion, cell membrane, cell wall, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, extracellular space, peroxisome, plastid and vacuole.

## Input

Enter a **Protein ID** and a complete protein sequence using the 20 standard one-letter amino-acid codes. Whitespace is removed automatically and non-standard characters are rejected.

Click **LOAD DEMO SEQUENCE** to test the module with the bundled plant-protein sequence.

## Advanced settings

The module exposes **Timeout (seconds)**, default 90, and **Allow the legacy server certificate**, enabled by default.

::: {.callout-warning}
Disabling certificate verification reduces transport security. Use it only for this legacy academic endpoint when normal validation fails, and do not submit confidential sequences to a service you do not trust.
:::

## Run the prediction

Click **PREDICT LOCALIZATION**. The result area reports status, protein ID/sequence length, number of predicted locations, prediction badges, result table, raw server response and method/publication information.

Use **DOWNLOAD RESULT** to save the parsed prediction as CSV.

## External-service limitation

Plant-mPLoc is not executed locally. Internet access and the availability/layout of the external server are required. If the server changes its HTML form or result page, ProtVis may receive a page but fail to identify the prediction. The **Raw response** tab is useful for troubleshooting.

## Programmatic use

```r
res <- ProtVis::predict_plant_mploc(
  sequence = my_sequence,
  id = "ZmProtein",
  timeout = 90,
  ignore_ssl = TRUE
)

res$prediction
```

When an active `ProtVis_dataset` exists, the GUI records the prediction as a schema-v4 analysis run with the protein ID, settings and result table.
